column3: Publishing "Tier A harm <= 1e-5" as a performance figure is an AI accuracy claim of the kind state AGs prosecute, and Texas TRAIGA lets the AG demand its basis
column5: An external-claims policy requiring any outside quotation of the metric to carry its exact definition, strata, exclusions and open items, with legal review and a ban on "X% compliant" phrasing.

column3: The success label is blind to complaints filed with regulators, the place where enforcement starts
column5: Feed served FCC informal complaints, ITG traceback notices and carrier blocking reports into the R115 intake bus, match them to sessions by number and time, and count each match as a Tier A candidate that triggers an audit surge.

column3: Carrier SMS enforcement (CTIA, A2P 10DLC) punishes the e-sign and "outbox copy" texts, and suspending the brand cuts off the only path to a signature
column5: Separate 10DLC/short-code campaigns per use case with CTIA-linted certified SMS templates, a use-case tag checked against campaign id, and a sender-health monitor that fails WAITING_FOR_SIGNATURE over to email and mail.

column3: Explainability demands meet discarded evidence: per-turn scores, speculative branches, pre-gate drops and redacted audio are exactly what explains a disputed decision, and they are gone
column5: A compact per-turn decision record (ASR n-best and confidences, pre-gate scores, top-k scores and margin, mask/threshold version, lexicon hits) kept with the R116 set so decisions stay explainable after raw-audio TTL, plus redaction span logs.

column3: Release cadence vs sample size: every content-hashed release needs ~300,000 fresh harm-free audited real calls before it can certify, so fixes cannot ship
column5: The monotone-patch class (superset stop set proven by replay over all retained audio inherits the Tier A certificate), plus sequential certification that carries evidence forward for states whose gold replay is unchanged, so routine releases do not each need ~300k fresh calls.

column3: Per-group release blockers at low volume: small dialect/accent groups can never reach the bound, so the release stalls or those groups get quietly dropped from the dial list
column4: Redefine per-group release blockers as the pooled absolute call-level bound plus per-group non-inferiority tests on turn-level Tier A rates, with a stated power analysis. A group with too little evidence gets acoustic-condition routing (low ASR confidence or worst cluster goes to a human), never exclusion. Extend the prohibited-basis build invariant to every campaign and dial-list selector (only consent, DNC, registration and suitability keys may filter), and add a reach-parity report comparing dialed share with the consent pool by census tract.

column3: Fair-lending matched-pair tests have no statistical power at campaign volume, and paired scripts cannot see outcome gaps that real-call error rates create
column5: Time-to-quote and quote-reached rate per acoustic cluster as a release blocker, and a pooled (hierarchical, multi-quarter) outcome-disparity review run with counsel.

column3: Human labelers' own miss rate puts a floor on the measurable harm rate; certifying 1e-5 needs a known labeler recall, meaning seeded gold harms and repeated independent listens that multiply audit cost
column5: Publish the Tier A bound divided by the lower confidence bound of measured labeler recall, plus a capture-recapture estimate across human, sweep and complaint channels.

column3: Certificate-expiry storms: lender rates and tariffs change weekly, every citing state expires at once, and fixed audit throughput can never re-certify financing states before the next change
column4: Type every policy-row change. A value-only change (same key, unit and authored spoken form, value inside the row's declared certified range, no new Reg Z trigger term) re-validates automatically through lints, calculator property tests, the R105 audio round-trip and bitwise gold replay, with no new audited calls. A structural change (new key, new wording, a value outside the range, a new trigger term) expires the certificate and needs audited recertification.

column3: The mandatory preamble produces mass short-duration hang-ups, and carrier analytics read those as spam, so "Spam Likely" labels crash answer rates and number rotation makes it worse
column5: Make short-call rate and analytics-label status per number a throttle input to the R138 dial permit, use a fixed registered number pool with per-number daily caps, and tell the lead the calling number and window at consent capture.

column3: A2P 10DLC daily caps and per-second throughput throttle the e-sign OTP SMS at the evening peak, so closes die while the customer waits on the line
column5: SMS capacity as an admission token reserved at QUOTE, priority classes in the outbox (OTP and envelope first), and carrier delivery receipts as WAITING_FOR events with vendor voice/email OTP fallback.

column3: Vendor-outage recovery flush: when the SMS/e-sign vendor comes back, the outbox drains hours of queued sends at midnight, outside texting hours and long after the calls
column4: Give every outbox SMS and email effect a [not_before, not_after] window, computed at enqueue by the pinned-tz calling-hours gate for the most restrictive candidate jurisdiction, and re-check it in the executor at send time. Add a model-checked invariant that no message effect is released outside its window. Never send expired session-bound items (OTP, envelope) late; re-plan them as one next-day, in-hours notice or a human callback. Rate-limit the drain after an outage and deduplicate it by idempotency key.

column3: Reassigned Numbers Database at scale: per-query cost on every dial attempt, "no data" responses that freeze whole lead segments, and RND downtime halting the campaign
column5: Batch-query the next day's dial list off-peak into a cache keyed by (number, consent date, RND data release), have the dial permit read it, and fail closed only when the current release cannot be confirmed.

column3: Correlated fallback surges at peak overwhelm human warm-transfer capacity: every uncertain path ends at a human, and the human floor must be staffed for the worst evening
column5: A human-capacity token in the dial permit (live fallback rate × transfer share vs staffed headroom), warm transfer only when a closer is free now, and otherwise an immediate concrete booked slot instead of hold audio.

column3: History pseudostates resume a stale substate after a GLOBAL detour without re-running the guard that first admitted it
column5: The lint banning shallow and deep history and forcing re-entry through the parent's guarded entry choice point, so the guarantee is explicit rather than implied.

column3: Timers live in user variables outside the graph, so a timer armed in one state fires after a GLOBAL exit into another
column5: A build-time fragment-to-state allowlist enforced by the renderer (fail closed), plus timers scoped to (state id, epoch) so leaving the arming state cancels them.

column3: Overlapping guards resolved by edge order: first-true-wins quietly picks the sale over the honest exit, and a diagram edit flips the order between releases
column4: Give suitability rows a fixed severity order (NOT_SUITABLE > ... > ROOF_FIRST > OK) with the table returning the most severe match, and add a build check (SMT over the abstract guard domain) that outgoing guards at every choice point are pairwise exclusive and jointly exhaustive, so behaviour-order numbers can never decide an outcome; replay a golden suitability suite every release with compliance sign-off on any changed outcome.

column3: Every commit passes READ_BACK is true but insufficient: the commit gate keys on a question id that is constant across read-backs, so a yes to an old read-back binds new terms
column5: Make the read-back question id instance-scoped (hash of quote hash plus nonce) so the binding is visible in the id itself.

column3: Counters reset on state entry plus data abstraction in the checker mean "clarify once, then fallback" and the call budgets never fire across a two-state ping-pong
column5: A lint that budget counters are root-owned and monotonic (increment-only), plus an independent runtime wall-clock watchdog outside StateSmith.

column3: GLOBAL exit sequences are not absorbing: root handlers stay live inside the stop/cancel exit, so a second GLOBAL event re-routes an opt-out back toward sales
column5: Put terminal exits in a region that does not inherit root GLOBAL sales handlers and state the invariant over the DNC flag rather than state names.

column3: Vacuous passes after a graph refactor: properties written against state names stay green when those states are split, renamed or bypassed
column5: Turn on vacuity checking (every antecedent needs a reachability witness) and write properties over derived predicates such as "state exposes a commit-class tool".

column3: An `else` / default branch on a choice point fails open when the policy table gains a value the graph was never generated for
column5: A build and runtime exhaustiveness check over every table-owned enum, with unknown values going fail-closed to human review, and a lint banning sales-forward `else` defaults at policy choice points.

column3: Exit and entry actions run on every path across a state boundary, so effects placed there fire on GLOBAL stop and cancel exits
column5: A lint banning effect intents in entry and exit actions, and a drain that re-reads the revocation ledger at send time and drops sales-purpose intents in any stop or cancel turn.

column3: Untimed model checking can't state or prove deadline properties, so the graph is "verified" while hard time limits are broken
column5: Have the dial permit refuse a dial when the remaining lawful window (most restrictive zone, Florida's 8 pm included) is shorter than the maximum call budget, and have the outbox refuse sales SMS after that deadline.

column3: Warm transfer as a harm sink: the release gate rewards Needle for handing the riskiest calls to humans, whose speech is outside the measured bound
column4: Define the audited "whole call trace" as the whole session including the recorded human leg (R203 softphone), count human-leg harm against the originating state's Tier A budget, and make a per-state fallback/transfer-rate ceiling (and any rise versus the previous release) a certification blocker so that lowering the clarify threshold to shed hard calls fails release.
column5: Report the audited harm rate of the transferred subpopulation separately in the R270 external-claims definition.

column3: The machine's compliance state is not handed over in a warm transfer: the human never sees the vulnerability counter, senior-cancel flag, jurisdiction or partial read-back
column5: State explicitly that any post-transfer close re-enters compiled READ_BACK/COMMIT and that a nonzero vulnerability counter sets no_same_call_close on the handoff.

column3: Fragment approvers sign off on isolated fragments, but regulators judge the net impression of the assembled call, which no human ever reviews
column4: Add a juxtaposition lint (aggregate social-proof fragments may not share a turn with, or come within N fragments of, any personalized price or savings fragment), a per-profile counsel-signed "path book" of coverage-sampled rendered fragment sequences as a release gate, and a "net impression misleading" label in the Tier A audit codebook.

column3: Audit labelers suffer psychological harm and turn over because the sampling plan routes the most distressing calls to them
column5: Use a specialist sensitive-content pool with transcript-first review, daily exposure caps, rotation and counseling, and report labeler tenure and gold accuracy per release.

column3: On-call alarm fatigue and kill-switch authority: per-state, per-group drift alarms get muted, and rollbacks get overridden under revenue pressure
column5: Put alarm thresholds and snooze settings in the content-hashed bundle (change = release with two-person compliance sign-off), and give no runtime override of Tier A reverts.

column3: Incentivized business owners edit the suitability and policy tables as "data changes" that bypass fragment-level legal review
column5: Add counsel-signed floors on suitability rows and a 100% independent-rubric audit of any newly admitted cohort after a loosening, and note that R258's auto-revalidation for value-only changes must not apply to suitability thresholds.

column3: Humans carry out the bot's booked callbacks and consults from their own phones and CRMs, outside the pre-dial gate
column5: Hide customer numbers from reps (softphone click-to-dial only), have a DNC or sweep hit cancel linked calendar items, and confirm consults by system SMS.

column3: The translation from legal sign-off to invariants is unreviewable: lawyers can't read the StateSmith graph or the temporal properties, and engineers make the legal interpretations
column4: Add a guard-to-statute traceability matrix. Every guard and invariant cites a regulation-profile row and carries counsel attestation over a generated plain-English rendering plus model-checker witness and counterexample transcripts. Replace "most restrictive wins" with union of obligations and intersection of permissions, with a satisfiability check that sends unsatisfiable jurisdiction mixes to lead-gen or a human.

column3: Harm labels are legal conclusions that crowd audio labelers aren't qualified to make, and lawyers can't listen at the volume certification needs
column5: Turn labels into factual codebook fields mapped to harm by a counsel-authored per-profile decision table, and measure labeler-to-attorney agreement on a random subsample each release.

column3: The humans the fallback relies on are deskilled by the automation (Bainbridge's "ironies of automation")
column5: Require transfer agents to hold a current certification keyed to the live policy-table version, and keep a minimum monthly live volume for them.

column3: Solar lease payment talk triggers Regulation M (Consumer Leasing Act) advertising disclosures, but the fragment lint only checks Reg Z co-occurrence
column4: Every typed financing row must name its advertising rule set (Reg Z for credit, Reg M 12 CFR 1013.7 for consumer leases under the ceiling, state lease rules) or the build fails; a Reg M co-occurrence lint forces any lease payment or down-payment phrase to render, in the same mandatory segment, that it is a lease, the total due at signing, the number and period of payments and any security deposit, all from table keys, with an undelivered segment (R39) triggering a written disclosure.
column5: Ban lease payment figures before QUOTE, as R32 already does for Reg Z trigger terms.

column3: Free add-on promotions (free EV charger, free critter guard, free first-year monitoring) whose cost is built into the per-watt price table
column5: Require an unbundled price row for every bundled add-on and a history check that blocks a promo if its base price row rose within the prior 30 days.

column3: Referral rewards pitched to the buyer as a way to pay off the system ("referral selling") are an unlawful inducement in home-improvement sales
column4: Give referral-reward keys a regulation-profile row (CA B&P 7157 and state referral-selling bans) and a model-checked invariant that no referral-reward fragment is reachable before signature plus the cancellation window (and never in banning states, only by separate outbox message elsewhere), plus a lint banning any fragment that pairs a payment or affordability key with a reward or promo key.
column5: Route affordability statements ("can't afford") to the R150 suitability check, never to objection handling.

column3: Product recalls hit SKUs that are already certified in the bundle: the agent keeps selling recalled equipment until a new bundle certifies
column5: A daily CPSC and manufacturer recall feed that sets supply_status=recalled automatically and fails closed, plus pre-dial suppression of marketing campaigns to owners of recalled units.

column3: Battery virtual-power-plant (VPP) income claims and third-party grid control are folded into the battery pitch with no read-back terms
column4: Type VPP rows as third_party_program; ban earnings fragments on the sales call; offer enrollment only after PTO by outbox under the program's own terms and consent; make a "programs may discharge your battery and reduce backup" limitation mandatory in READ_BACK whenever a battery is quoted, and flag outage_backup plus any program default as a product-fit conflict.
column5: Warranty rows state throughput limits and whether program cycling counts against them.

column3: Add-on and expansion upsells to existing solar owners forfeit their grandfathered net-metering tariff
column4: Add a tariff_vintage slot (legacy tariff, interconnection date, grandfather end) from the utility API and interconnection agreement, per-utility expansion_rule rows, a whole-system calculator delta including lost legacy-tariff value, sizing capped at the threshold or NOT_SUITABLE when the delta is negative, no figure when vintage is unknown, and a mandatory READ_BACK row when the add-on crosses the threshold.
column5: Keep existing-customer upsell campaigns in lead-gen mode until that profile is certified.

column3: Same menu for all (the fair-lending invariant) collides with product legality that varies by state: third-party PPAs are unlawful in some states
column5: A default-deny product_legality row per (financing type, state, utility territory) with a legal attestation, and a model-checked invariant that QUOTE offers exactly the attested lawful set for the property's jurisdiction.

column3: Bundled recurring services (monitoring, maintenance plans, panel cleaning, extended warranty) auto-renew on the single lexical COMMIT
column4: Type recurring or auto-renewing rows as negative_option and bar them from voice QUOTE and READ_BACK; sell them only in writing through an ARL/ROSCA flow with clear terms, a separate affirmative checkbox and signature, an acknowledgment and an online cancel path; give cancel_or_rescind a target (contract or plan); lint "renews" tokens out of voice fragments.

column3: Roofing and electrical bundles sold under a solar contractor's licence class that doesn't cover those trades
column4: Give every quote line item and change order a required_license_class per jurisdiction, extend the R178 invariant so each needs a matching valid class on the contracting licensee's row (or an attested incidental-work rule), split the contract otherwise, and name the licensee and licence number per line item in READ_BACK and the contract.

column3: Deterministic "limited-time" and "showcase home" promotions become rolling, perpetual deadlines: false scarcity certified as fact
column5: A build check over table history rejecting promos re-issued with a new end date within 12 months.

column3: Anger with no opt-out word: hostile venting has no event, so "clarify once, then fallback" makes a furious caller repeat the rant, then books another call
column4: Add a GLOBAL call_frequency_complaint/hostility class (lexicon plus Needle: "keep calling", "Nth call this week", "stop harassing", "you people") that counts as revocation by reasonable means. It writes DNC through the R115 bus and plays a fixed apology-and-end fragment. Add a model-checked invariant that no callback or consult effect is reachable after a negative-valence, complaint or hostility turn, so the out_of_scope fallback there ends with suppression. Change the R167 negative-valence fragment so it never offers another call. Add a red-team stratum of non-lexical hostile revocations with a Tier A false-continue bound.
column5: Make the clarify for a high-ASR-confidence out_of_scope the R24 check question ("keep going, or let you go?") rather than "say that again".

column3: Conversational "stop" ("wait, stop, go back to the price") trips the union stop lexicon, and the caller's "no, keep going" can't legally undo it
column5: Name "stop" plus a repair cue ("go back", "what was", "really?") as an explicit Tier 2 pattern, with a per-marker false-stop release bound.

column3: Crying, sighing and groaning are dropped as non-speech, so the bot's first reply to a sobbing person is "I didn't catch that"
column4: Add a pinned, per-utterance, non-identifying non-speech vocalization detector (sob, sigh, laugh, groan) that complies with R118 and runs before the pre-gate. A sob or sustained voiced non-speech turn routes to sensitive_event(distress) with a fixed "Take your time, is this a bad moment? I can let you go" fragment, no pitch and no same-call close. A following "never mind"/acknowledge counts as indirect_decline. Add per-stratum certification bounds and a rendered-crying red-team stratum as release blockers.

column3: Joking hyperbole in qualifying answers is grounded as a literal slot value ("roof's older than me", "a million trees")
column5: A NOT_SUITABLE resting only on a spoken slot that conflicts with permit or aerial records should go to survey, never to an honest exit.

column3: Haggling: the agent has no authority to concede, so negotiators are routed to humans who can discount, and price ends up depending on assertiveness
column4: Use one pricing authority. The closer CRM has no free price field, and any human concession is an R37 policy row applied by the same calculator with a reason code and evidence id, producing a new quote hash, a READ_BACK/written re-disclosure and R134 monitor coverage. Offer any concession row to every buyer who qualifies, and add haggle and request-human arms to the matched-pair tests, with price gaps between arms counted as Tier A fair-lending harm.

column3: Condition laundering: the closed re-ask after a conditional yes drops the condition, and the caller's next "yes" still assumes it
column4: Add a condition_stated(topic) event. Before any re-ask, a fixed policy-table fragment answers the condition ("Installation is estimated <range>; we can't promise earlier", "<add_on> is not included", or "The contract includes only what I read"). Any unmet condition blocks a same-call close and leads to a written proposal listing what is not included, plus a consult. Log customer-asserted conditions for the R144 post-sign check, and add a Tier A stratum of a conditional affirm followed by a bare yes.

column3: A soft retraction seconds after the commit ("...hm, actually, let me sleep on it") has no event, because nothing has been signed yet to cancel
column4: In CONTRACT_SENT and WAITING_FOR_SIGNATURE, map defers_decision, indirect_decline or a hesitation lexicon hit ("think about it", "sleep on it", "hold on, actually") to an envelope void through the vendor API, with a fixed "No problem, I've withdrawn the link, nothing was signed" fragment and a written proposal. Add an invariant of no sign prompt and no reminder after a defer, release the envelope only after the commit turn's endpointing plus the R173 listen window, and track signature after an in-call retraction as a Tier A metric.

column3: Interruptions during READ_BACK: the design never defines whether to resume or restart, and both choices break the commit
column5: A single uninterrupted recap before the commit question after any digression, and keep READ_BACK repair turns out of the R69 turn budget.

column3: Meta-questions testing the bot ("is a real person listening?", "will you learn from this call?", "are you reading a script?") have no events, and the truthful answers are yes
column5: A GLOBAL data_use_question event whose fixed answer names live listening (none), human quality review and model-improvement use, and routes to decline_recording.

column3: Storytellers run out the call budget: time and turn counters fire WRAP_UP mid-anecdote on engaged buyers, mostly older ones
column5: Count budgets on agent-side loops rather than caller talk time, and route budget exhaustion with no negative signal to a booked consult at a named time.

column3: E-sign OTP and "outbox copy" texts to a Canadian (+1) mobile fall under Canada's anti-spam law (CASL), which the compliance gates never model
column4: Resolve every outbound number from NPA to country (with a carrier lookup) before any SMS or email effect. Treat Canadian and Caribbean NPAs as foreign jurisdictions. With no certified CASL profile, the outbox refuses and signing falls back to mail or consultant-assisted signing. Add a build check that every outbox fragment carries the profile's required identification and unsubscribe keys.
column5: Model-check that no SMS effect exists for a number whose country is unresolved.

column3: Booked callbacks and warm-transfer follow-ups to Canadian numbers trigger the CRTC telemarketing regime (DNCL registration, Canadian calling hours, ADAD rules)
column4: Any candidate jurisdiction without a certified regulation profile is a hard no-dial and no-SMS. This covers any non-US country, whether identified by NPA or by stated location. callback_request is refused at booking with a fixed fragment and a written follow-up instead. Add the invariant that no callback books to an unprofiled jurisdiction.

column3: US territories: Puerto Rico's net-metering law is under a federal oversight board's lawsuit, so a territory's "certified" policy-table row can be voided by PROMESA litigation, not by legislative change
column5: A legal_basis and docket-watch field on statute-backed rows that marks contested rows as assumption-only, and territories as lead-gen until a profile is certified.

column3: Day-of-week and legal-holiday telemarketing bans, including parish-only holidays and territory dates across the International Date Line, absent from a pre-dial gate built on hours and frequency
column4: Add calendar_rule rows (day-of-week bans and legal-holiday lists) to each profile. Give each holiday a geographic scope (state, parish or county, municipality) resolved from the parcel geocode, and treat unknown scope as statewide. Evaluate every candidate zone on its local date. Add a full-year property test and the invariant that no DIAL happens on a banned local date.

column3: Sub-state licensing: home improvement contractor and salesperson licences required by New York City and by suburban counties where the state has none, so a lead-gen mode keyed by state misses them
column4: Make the regulation profile a layer stack (state, county, municipality, tribal) resolved from the parcel geocode, with contractor and salesperson rows allowed on any layer. A locality whose licensing coverage isn't attested defaults to lead-gen. Add the invariant that no on-call price is given unless every layer's salesperson row permits it.

column3: Address-level tax jurisdiction: the "total cost" read back depends on home-rule city and county sales-tax options and on ZIP codes that straddle city lines
column5: A rooftop-geocode tax_jurisdiction slot with local exemption rows, so the quoted price is accurate rather than merely honored.

column3: Municipal utilities and electric co-ops are exempt from state net-metering statutes, and their service territories don't follow city, ZIP or county lines
column5: Co-op and municipal tariff rows must cite the board's own tariff, with a short effective_until and a board-meeting monitor.

column3: Snowbird seasonal vacancy: a part-year home produces most when it is empty, and annual true-up or avoided-cost cash-outs erase the credits the savings figure assumes
column5: A build check that every tariff row has true-up period, carryover and cash-out rate fields, plus a neutral year-round occupancy question.

column3: Cancellation-window arithmetic: "midnight of the third business day" depends on the buyer's state holiday calendar and on time-zone lines inside states and reservations
column5: A single certified deadline function using the parcel's zone and the union of federal, state and local holidays.

column3: Border towns: rural mailing addresses use a post office across the state line, so the lead record puts the house in the wrong state and nothing in the call ever corrects it
column4: A pre-dial resolver geocodes to a rooftop point and then a parcel (state, county, municipality, AHJ, tribal, tax and utility territory). Postal city and state are never the jurisdiction key. If postal and parcel states disagree, both become candidates with most-restrictive-wins, and there is no close until a human confirms the parcel. The utility API's service address must match the parcel state.

column3: The self-echo filter deletes caller speech that matches the agent's own audio, so a "stop" timed to the agent's word "stop" (or spoken in a cloned agent voice) is removed as echo
column4: The echo filter may never discard a stop, cancel or DNC lexicon token: any matched span containing one is treated as overlap residue (R24 check question at once, number suppress-pending until human review). Near-end energy above a double-talk threshold is never classed as echo. The post-call sweep runs on the raw pre-filter ASR, and the opt-out sentence is linted so "stop" is not its final word.
column5: A red-team stratum of stop words timed over the agent's own matching words, with a Tier A false-continue bound.

column3: The media/far-field detector can be fooled into classing the caller's own voice as TV/radio, so their stop and rescind turns are thrown away
column5: A model-checked invariant that no front-end tag (media, echo, no-speech) can keep text from the lexicon and GLOBAL stop pass.

column3: No liveness check: replayed "yes" clips, a soundboard or a cloned owner voice pass IDENTITY and the COMMIT gate on a spoofed inbound call
column5: Never pay lead partners on verbal commits, appointments or callback requests, only on independently labeled installed outcomes.

column3: Regex denial of service: crafted long turns make the canonicalizer's or stop lexicon's dialect patterns backtrack exponentially, stalling the turn pipeline
column4: Compile every lexicon, canonicalizer and redactor pattern to a linear-time automaton (RE2/Hyperscan class) with a build check banning backreferences and lookaround and CI worst-case runtime fuzzing; cap per-turn front-end input length; run each session's front end under a CPU quota with a hard deadline, where a missed deadline fails toward the R24 check question plus suppress-pending.
column5: A per-ANI front-end latency monitor feeding the inbound rate limiter.

column3: Spoken prompt injection against the big model while it is the live stand-in classifier and labeler in the build phase
column5: An injection-phrase lexicon that sends the call to full human audit and bars that call's teacher labels from training.

column3: The payment-data redactor's greedy digit matching deletes the phone numbers and opt-out words inside a DNC request before Needle, the lexicon and the post-call sweep see them
column4: Tighten the card pattern (Luhn plus valid IIN, never spanning a non-digit word, NANP 10-digit groups excluded), and run a deterministic in-memory dnc_number extractor on raw ASR before redaction whenever a stop token occurs in the turn, writing each named number to the DNC ledger through the R115 bus; any redacted turn containing a stop token keeps the number suppress-pending until compliance reviews the R273 span log.
column5: Confirm the suppressed numbers back to the caller in the outbox text.

column3: An availability attack on certification: coordinated callers feed crafted near-tie utterances to drive a state's live error bound and drift alarms over threshold, forcing fleet-wide fallback or rollback
column5: Attribute audited errors to source clusters (ANI range, consent source, carrier route) so a concentrated breach quarantines that cluster instead of the whole fleet.

column3: The speculative cache and clarify behaviour leak Needle's confidence through response latency, giving attackers a cheap oracle to map decision boundaries
column5: Quantize reply onset per state so speculation hit, miss and clarify are indistinguishable in timing.

column3: Lead-record name slots spoken by the agent become commands to smart speakers in the callee's room
column5: List every assistant wake word and its phonetic neighbours explicitly in the R62 blocklist, checked on the ASR round-trip of the rendered audio.

column3: Selective jamming: a second person times noise over the owner's objections, so the ASR-confidence pre-gate discards them and the jammer answers the closed re-ask
column5: Count speech-present turns rejected by the pre-gate in QUALIFY/READ_BACK/COMMIT, and block a same-call close after one until a human has heard those spans.

column3: Teacher-student capacity gap: a frontier teacher is the wrong teacher for a 26M student, and hard event labels throw away what little it could pass on
column5: Add a per-state learning-curve check (no audited gain over two data doublings means stop adding data and split the question or keep the fallback), plus soft targets from an offline teacher-assistant model.

column3: Retiring the big model deletes the second opinion that drives audit sampling and DAgger, so post-retirement audits are random-only and lose almost all detection power
column5: Relabel retired-state transcripts nightly with the offline big model and a second model family, send their disagreements to the audit queue, and give every call later linked to a rescind or complaint a 100% audit.

column3: Privileged-information teacher: the big model labels turns using whole-call context that Needle never sees, so identical Needle inputs carry contradictory labels
column5: Use observation-matched labeling, where the teacher and humans see Needle's exact view and a separate field records the whole-call reading, plus a per-release detector that collapses identical (state, text) pairs with conflicting labels to clarify.

column3: RLHF-tuned generators collapse paraphrase diversity, so synthetic "coverage" is dense around fluent typical phrasings and empty where real callers talk
column5: Measure coverage as the nearest-neighbour distance from real build-phase turns to the training set, broken out by length and token shape, and seed generation for uncovered regions with real fragments.

column3: A 26M model cannot hold the domain's entity knowledge (utilities, CCAs, co-ops, roof materials, lenders), and the grounding gate checks only that a string was said, not that it maps to the right key
column5: Move entity canonicalization into a deterministic alias resolver (EIA-861 utilities, CCAs, retail providers) filtered to the geocoded territory, where zero or several matches lead to clarify.

column3: PII scrubbing of seed transcripts deletes the very spans Needle must learn to extract as slots, and LLM-filled surrogates don't look like real ones
column5: Use shape-preserving surrogates sampled from real verbalization patterns and census name lists, plus a release check comparing slot-shape histograms between real gold and training data.

column3: Margin and softmax thresholds are tuned on synthetic held-out data, and a small model's calibration collapses under shift, so "clarify" fires least where Needle is most wrong
column5: Check selective risk per stratum at the chosen threshold, and add a divergence alarm for clarify rate falling while hang-ups or out_of_scope rise.

column3: The build-phase data captures callers adapting to big-model latency, a conversational rhythm that disappears once fast Needle runs
column5: Tag build-phase turns with the preceding agent gap and down-weight turns after gaps over 700 ms. Compare turn-length and overlap distributions between the build phase and the canary before widening the ramp.

column3: Label-by-construction: generated hard cases drift off the event they were requested for, and synthetic data underperforms most on subjective boundaries like affirm vs acknowledge vs unclear
column5: Relabel generated boundary items blind with a different model family, and block release for any class whose label-noise rate, measured on a blind human sample, is above threshold.

column3: Underspecification: training runs with equal offline scores behave differently on real callers, so which weights enter real-call audit is a coin flip the synthetic suite can't call
column5: Train K seeds, select by the worst case over the stress suites, track seed churn on real gold as a release metric, and run GLOBAL as an OR-ensemble of seeds (a monotone superset under R254).

column3: Speculation shaves the wrong latency: the endpointing silence timeout, not Needle or TTS, sets the reply gap, and Tier A states lengthen it
column5: The silence-onset precompute and a per-state "caller-perceived gap" plus "hello?"/re-speak rate metric, so the trade-off in Tier A states is measured, not assumed.

column3: Cache misses land on objections and money questions, so the agent's delays fall exactly where human listeners read delay as evasion or bad news
column5: The defense's onset-by-event-class test should be folded into R301's CI test, and the defense should have cited R301 rather than proposing it as new.

column3: Safety exits are never pre-rendered: stop, cancel and request_human are rare, so they are never in top-k and always take the slowest path
column5: Keep GLOBAL exit fragments resident in the playout buffer and give exit onset its own p99 bound.

column3: The longer Tier A endpoint wait after the closing question copies the "silent close" pressure tactic
column5: A fixed "No rush, you can also get this in writing" fragment on a silence(duration_bucket) event in AWAIT_CONFIRM, and hedge tokens added to the hesitation lexicon.

column3: The agent never backchannels, so on a phone line its silence during long caller turns sounds like a dropped call
column4: Add a certified continuer set ("mm-hm", "I see", "go on", no assent words) that plays only in intra-turn pauses scored non-final by incomplete(), after about 6 s of caller speech, never over voiced frames and never in AWAIT_CONFIRM. Add a channel_check event that answers "Yes, I'm here, go ahead" and keeps the long turn open so the R44 merger joins both sides. Exclude channel_check from the R107 "hello?" counter, and add a fragmentation-rate bound on a long-narrative stratum.

column3: Barge-in and backchannel are not told apart during agent playback, so habitual "mm-hm"s chop every fragment
column4: Duck-then-decide: a burst during playback ducks audio and holds it for up to about 400 ms while the lexicon classifies the residue. A short backchannel with no stop-adjacent token resumes from the current clause and keeps the delivered flag. Anything else stops playout and goes to PAUSE as now. After 3 backchannel overlaps, switch to short chunks with pauses (the R238 profile). Backchannel overlaps don't count toward the R152 barge-in signal. Add a high-backchannel stratum with per-group completion and replay bounds as release blockers.

column3: Simultaneous-start collisions: after a gap, the caller and the agent start together, both stop, and the agent restarts its fragment from the top
column5: Deterministic backoff on repeated collisions (a longer silent window after each yield) and a per-call collision-rate drift metric.

column3: A barge-in on a half-played question binds the caller's answer to a question they never fully heard, especially "A or B" questions
column5: A fragment lint against "A or B" slot and offer questions, and a played_fraction field on slot provenance.

column3: Trail-off turns ("but...", "so...", "I mean...") are finished turns, but dangling-word endpointing treats them as incomplete(), so caller and agent both wait
column5: A trail-off class (turn-final "but/so/I mean/though" with level or falling prosody ends the turn after about 700 ms) that routes to the indirect_decline question in READ_BACK and COMMIT.

column3: The "speculation on/off gives bit-identical committed traces" CI check is open-loop, so it cannot see how reply timing changes what the caller says next
column5: Stratify the audited harm measure by speculation mode and reply-gap bucket, and run a small randomized speculation-off holdout arm.

column3: The symmetric near-tie rule treats a stop-vs-continue tie like any other tie, so a probable opt-out gets "could you say that again?" instead of a stop
column5: The stop-suspect band (sub-threshold stop mass goes to the R24 check question, never a generic "say that again") and the "quit" family in Tier 1, expanded through the R277 confusion model.

column3: The clarify re-ask produces hyperarticulated repetition that the pinned ASR recognizes worse, so "clarify once" makes the second try less likely to succeed than the first
column5: A post-clarify certification stratum with per-group bounds, and offering DTMF in the same breath on numeric re-asks.

column3: Model uncertainty is billed to the caller: Needle's own near-ties and clarifies are indistinguishable from caller confusion, so they drive "rising confusion" and the vulnerability counter
column4: The vulnerability counter takes only caller-content signals (confused(), contradictions between committed slots, wrong_party_reference, R152 overcommitment). Margin near-ties, OOD-floor unclear and grounding misses go to a separate model_uncertainty counter that routes to a human or ACCESS_PATH as an access failure, never to NO_SALE_SAFE_EXIT, never suppresses redial and never disables speculation as a "confusion" signal.

column3: The "live error bound" can only run on real-time confidence proxies (clarify and near-tie rates), and those proxies reward confidently wrong states and punish careful ones
column5: A per-state "high-confidence decision later contradicted" rate (read-back corrections, dispute_prior_statement, role-binding disagreement) and an explicit audit surge on any post-release drop in clarify or near-tie rate.

column3: The gate thresholds themselves (margin, softmax floor, ASR-confidence cutoff, vulnerability count, call budgets) aren't listed in the content-hashed certified bundle, so they can be changed without recertifying
column4: Make every gate parameter (margin, softmax/OOD floor, ASR and word-confidence floors, veto threshold, vulnerability counts, call budgets, endpointing timers) a compile-time constant in the generated C, included in the bundle hash and certificate key, with no runtime config path and a build check that fails if any guard reads a non-hashed value.

column3: The ASR-confidence pre-gate scores whole utterances, so a confident average hides the one low-confidence word that decides the turn
column5: A word-level confidence floor on pivotal tokens (digits, negations, modals) with n-best polarity disagreement forcing a contrastive clarify, plus a can/can't, fifteen/fifty minimal-pair audio stratum.

column3: Fallback to a booked callback sends the caller back into the same uncertain state with the same weights, which creates a clarify-fail-callback loop that burns frequency caps and consent
column4: Write a lead-level failed_state record (state id plus bundle hash) on any clarify-then-fallback; the R138 dial permit refuses any AI redial that would re-enter that state under the same or an equivalent bundle, so follow-up is only a human, DTMF/SMS self-serve or a written proposal, and the fallback fragment says plainly that a person will follow up.

column3: The slot store has no UNKNOWN value, so a caller's honest "I don't know" about roof age, shade or move horizon is forced into a typed value, a clarify loop, or a guard default
column4: Add a dont_know(slot) event and an UNKNOWN value for every QUALIFY slot, a caller_estimate provenance for hedged answers, and mandatory suitability-table rows for UNKNOWN and near-cutoff estimates that resolve via permit/aerial records to ROOF_FIRST or NOT_SUITABLE (build check enforces the rows); no clarify asks for a number after the caller says they don't know.

column3: One-hot training labels from the big model and from single annotators teach Needle that no utterance is ambiguous, so the near-tie rule rarely fires on genuinely ambiguous turns
column5: Soft-label targets from two-auditor disagreement and K-teacher sampling, with calibration error on high-disagreement items as a per-state release metric.

column3: Explicit confirmation ("Did you say fifteen?") turns misrecognitions into "customer-confirmed" facts, because callers accept wrong echoes and the "yes" then becomes the provenance
column5: A separate agent_echo_confirmed provenance and contrastive n-best confirmation ("one-fifty, two-fifty, or something else?") instead of single-value echoes.

column3: The COMMIT gate rejects the natural, enthusiastic yes, so the most willing buyers get re-asked and then pushed to fallback
column5: A per-dialect "clear assent, re-asked" false-reject metric at COMMIT as a release blocker, plus a certified set of action-phrase variants ("send it", "send it over") accepted only when the clause carries no negation, conditional or reported-speech marker.

column3: Read-first buyers: no path sends a written proposal before the verbal commit, so "email me the numbers, I'll sign tonight" ends the sale
column5: An explicit request_written_proposal() event in QUOTE, READ_BACK and COMMIT, and a short verified return path (inbound or booked callback, OTP, then READ_BACK) with proposal-path conversion tracked.

column3: Audio-only READ_BACK of nine dense numeric categories exceeds listener working memory, so willing buyers stall, ask for repeats or drop
column5: Send a link-free written terms sheet matching the read-back to every buyer at READ_BACK entry, not only in CAPTION_MODE, and lint segments to at most three numbers each.

column3: The e-sign link arrives as a cold text from an unknown number carrying a link and an OTP: the exact smishing pattern phones and the agent itself teach people to ignore
column5: A fixed fragment naming the sender and first words before the send, plus an on-call "did the text arrive?" check that routes "no" to a fixed tip about the filtered or unknown-senders folder.

column3: Credit freezes block the lender's pull after the commit, and the design has no event, fragment or step to get them lifted
column5: A file_frozen lender status with a fixed, compliance-approved "lift the freeze and reopen the same link" fragment, an outbox copy of the lender link valid until quote expiry, and a booked callback.

column3: A pending refinance, home purchase or HELOC collides with new solar debt and the UCC fixture filing; QUALIFY never asks
column5: Reword R208 to name home-equity loans, other home purchases and anything in progress now, with a pending_mortgage_activity row that means no same-call close.

column3: Two calculators: the read-back's payment and total come from the policy-table calculator, but the signed documents come from the lender's amortization engine
column5: Have the lender API return the exact TILA box for the funded amount, speak the no-autopay APR and payment as primary, and run a to-the-cent pre-send check of envelope fields against the read-back values.

column3: The utility account holder isn't a record owner (late spouse, adult child, ex), so the interconnection paperwork has no valid signer
column4: Add an interconnection_signer slot written only by the utility authorization API. If the account holder is not a signing record owner, block the same-call close, send a written proposal stating that a utility account transfer is required, and have a human consult handle the transfer. Make the utility interconnection application a required signer role in the envelope, and block install until the utility confirms the account holder has signed.

column3: Lead-record errors make genuine, willing owners fail the IDENTITY challenge-response, which sends them to WRONG_PARTY
column5: Measure the false-WRONG_PARTY bound on live audited calls per dialect, and send lead-versus-record mismatches to a vendor data-quality metric.

column3: NOT_SUITABLE counts as success, so false-negative suitability exits of good buyers are invisible to the metric and to certification
column5: A sampled false-NOT_SUITABLE audit against an independent rubric with a per-row over-exit bound as a release blocker, and hedged answers that straddle a threshold routed to a survey rather than an exit.

column3: State ADAD statutes (California PUC 2874) require a live, unrecorded natural-voice announcement and consent before any recorded message plays
column5: An explicit adad_rule row per profile that records the consent-path basis (PUC 2873 / 2872(f)) and blocks dialing where consent is missing or a layer has no consent alternative, rather than adding a human live-intro operator.

column3: Every artificial-voice call must state the seller's callback telephone number (47 CFR 64.1200(b)(2)); the preamble has no such segment
column4: Add a callback_number policy key: a staffed line, not the dialed ANI, that accepts DNC requests and is live-tested daily. Make it a profile-mandated preamble segment (counted only on uninterrupted playback) and repeat it in every agent-initiated END fragment. Add a model-checked invariant that no path from DISCLOSED reaches an agent hang-up without a playout mark on it, proven per call through the R116 render log.

column3: Aggregate social proof computed over success-labeled customers is survivorship-filtered review data under the FTC's 2024 Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule
column5: A typed sampling_frame on every review or satisfaction aggregate, with a build check that rejects frames filtered on outcome, satisfaction or complaint status (it must be all signed contracts, cancelled included, with the response rate stated).

column3: FTC Holder Rule: seller-arranged solar loans must carry the Holder notice, which turns every certified spoken claim into a defense against the lender
column4: Hash each admitted lender loan-document version into the bundle. Admit a lender program only if the verbatim 433.2 notice is present and no recovery-cap pattern appears (extend the R222 lint to lender docs). At runtime, refuse CONTRACT_SENT and accept no milestone funding unless the lender envelope's document hash matches an admitted version.

column3: Credit-filtered lead lists and pre-call lender soft pulls are FCRA consumer reports used for marketing without a firm offer of credit
column5: A required selection_criteria field on each lead-source attestation that rejects any credit-derived criterion, plus a build check that no pre-dial job calls a bureau or lender API.

column3: TSR external-upsell rules: ROOF_FIRST, partner roofing, batteries and lead-gen handoffs to partner installers are a second seller in the same call with no new seller disclosure
column5: A model-checked invariant that no effect whose counterparty differs from the preamble seller can fire during a live call without a compiled seller-change disclosure and a lexical affirm.

column3: The opt-out confirmation text is narrowly limited by the FCC's 2024 revocation rules (one text, within 5 minutes, no marketing), and the outbox can't meet that
column5: A dedicated revocation_confirmation template with not_after = revocation time + 5 minutes, top priority class, dropped rather than sent late, and one per revocation.

column3: State mini-TCPA consent-form elements (Florida FTSA 501.059, Oklahoma, Maryland) aren't met by a consent check that only verifies "seller + AI voice"
column4: Add consent_form_element rows to each profile layer (FL 501.059 technology wording, authorized number, not-a-condition, and the OK and MD analogues). Have a counsel-maintained registry classify each consent disclosure-text hash against every layer's elements, and make the R138 dial permit require the hash to be approved for every candidate jurisdiction (unknown hash = no dial).

column3: Drip and partitioned pricing: quoting per-watt or monthly figures before the all-in total violates Massachusetts 940 CMR 38 and California SB 478
column4: Type fee rows as mandatory or optional, and add a calculator build check that folds every mandatory fee into total_price (nothing mandatory may appear only in the envelope). Add a fragment-sequence invariant that the first price-typed fill in any call is total_price, with monthly figures allowed only inside the same fragment, and ban per-watt keys from voice in every profile.

column3: New York's Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure Act: a price computed from the caller's personal data needs the statutory "set by an algorithm" disclosure, and no fragment has it
column4: Add an algorithmic_pricing_disclosure key with the verbatim statutory text to the NY layer, with a co-occurrence lint that places it in the same fragment as every calculator_output price fill, spoken and written. Add a legislative-change monitor with an attestation effective_until date per profile layer, so a new statute or a lapsed re-attestation drops the layer to lead-gen (no price) until counsel re-attests.

column3: The compiled preamble order puts the opt-out announcement far more than two seconds after the identification, as 64.1200(b)(3) requires for artificial-voice calls
column4: Make the (b)(3) profile row place the opt-out clause immediately after the seller name inside segment 1. Add a build check that sums the pre-rendered clip durations (R105) between the end of the identification and the start of the opt-out and fails above 1.5 s, add a per-call playout-mark check that flags any breach as a Tier A harm, and add the deadline to the timed model.
column5: Make the same timing invariant cover NEW_PARTY replays and the abbreviated replay after barge-in.

column3: An opt-out spoken before the preamble: the unskippable preamble either pitches after the stop or ends the call without the identification every artificial-voice call must give
column4: Compile every TERMINAL fragment that can be the first agent speech to begin with the seller identity and callback number, enforced by a lint on the seller and callback keys. Add a model-checked invariant that every path from a human answer to HANGUP plays an identification-bearing fragment, and send a DNC confirmation SMS naming the seller.

column3: Garbled first words trigger the root-level clarify/unintelligible re-ask in OPENING, so the bot's first words are "Sorry, I didn't catch that" and not who is calling
column5: A model-checked "first audio" invariant: the first agent fragment on an answered call is PREAMBLE segment 1, an identity-bearing TERMINAL fragment or the VOICEMAIL message.

column3: Front-end clipping at answer: the callee's first syllables are lost while the media path comes up, so "Don't call..." reaches Needle as "call..." and "No, I'm not interested" as "I'm interested"
column5: Buffer early media from 200 OK and flag onset-truncated first turns with stop-adjacent residue for the R24 check question and suppress-pending.

column3: A child answers and the non-owner handling asks when a parent will be home, getting and storing "I'm home alone till six"
column5: A lint banning any fragment that asks about another person's whereabouts or return time, plus a minor/alone lexicon that ends the call and quarantines the span in the same way as R119.

column3: Wait-for-callee records and analyzes the callee's greeting and room audio before the recording notice plays
column5: A pre-notice quarantine in every jurisdiction: audio before the recording-notice playout mark feeds only the live stop pass and the teardown sweep, and is never retained, labeled or trained on.

column3: Institutional greetings (hospital, nursing home, care facility or business switchboard) have no event, so the bot runs the sales preamble and asks to be put through to the resident
column5: A GLOBAL institutional_answer event (facility or switchboard greeting) that ends the call without asking for anyone, plus pre-dial suppression of numbers on licensed-facility registries.

column3: An opt-out spoken by the callee's machine (screening assistant quick reply or the outgoing greeting) at the opening is routed to screener/voicemail handling, outside the stop union
column5: State explicitly that the post-call sweep covers greeting and screener legs, and add an OS screening canned-reply red-team stratum.

column3: Whispered answers ("I'm in a meeting / the baby's asleep, not now") fall below the VAD and ASR pre-gate, and the bot answers a whisper at full volume
column4: Add a non-identifying unvoiced-speech detector ahead of the pre-gate so a whisper is never treated as silence or a timeout. End the call on a detected whisper with a fixed low-gain exit, count it as indirect_decline, and put the number under suppress-pending until a human has reviewed the span. Add a whispered-speech certification stratum with Tier A false-continue bounds.

column3: Anti-robocall tones played by a live callee (SIT "disconnected" tri-tone, TeleZapper-style) are taken as a network event, so a deliberate opt-out becomes a "bad number"
column5: Treat an in-band SIT after answer supervision and near-end speech as callee_device_objection (internal DNC), and never as a vacated-number signal.
